summary: Main JPEG marker parsing dispatcher. While the current marker slot a1[94] (offset this+0x178) is non-zero it dispatches on the marker value: markers 192..204 and 1 route through ImageFormatStreamDecoder, sub_510975, or sub_510ACC; markers 205..207, 197..200 and 195 route to the error dispatch (state code 59 via obj vfunc0); markers 1 and 208..215 route to the parameterized dispatch (state code 91 via obj vfunc1); 216 (SOI) calls sub_50FF84; 217 sets state code 84 via obj vfunc1 and returns 2; 219 calls MP3HuffmanDecoder; 220/221 call StreamingDataReader / StreamRead2ByteTokenParser; 224..239 (APP) dispatch through a function table at this+0x190; 254 (COM) dispatches through the handler at *(this+0x190+12) (this+0x19C); unrecognized markers write state code 67 and dispatch through obj vfunc0. When a1[94] is zero the next marker is read through BitstreamTokenReader or JPEGMarkerReader selected by the byte-stuffing flag at *(this+0x190+0x50). The marker slot is reset to 0 after every dispatch.

local_names.a1: this: _DWORD* stream/parse context (a1[94] = marker at offset 0x178, a1[100] = dispatch/reader config pointer at offset 0x190)
local_names.obj: state dispatcher object at *this (obj+0x14 state code, obj+0x18 marker value, vfunc0/vfunc1 dispatchers)
local_names.v2: current marker value (a1[94]) used as the dispatch key
local_names.v3: per-marker parser/handler result; 0 aborts the loop
local_names.v4/v5/v6: decremented marker-distance values used to route markers 201..205
local_names.v8: bit-stream flag passed to ImageFormatStreamDecoder for markers 192/193 (0) and 201 (1)

operations.description: Read the next marker when the marker slot a1[94] is zero: select BitstreamTokenReader when the byte-stuffing flag byte at *(a1[100]+80) is set, otherwise JPEGMarkerReader
Return 0 when the marker reader returns 0
Branch on the current marker value a1[94]: values above 207 leave the inner loop for the high-marker dispatch block
Error dispatch for markers 205..207, 197..200 and 195: write state code 59 to obj+0x14, the marker to obj+0x18, and dispatch through obj vtable slot 0
Marker 202 dispatches to ImageFormatStreamDecoder(1, this, 1) and marker 204 to sub_510975
Markers 192 and 193 dispatch to ImageFormatStreamDecoder(0, this, 0) and marker 201 to ImageFormatStreamDecoder(0, this, 1)
Marker 194 dispatches to ImageFormatStreamDecoder(1, this, 0) and marker 196 to sub_510ACC
Return 0 when the selected per-marker parser returns 0
Reset the marker slot a1[94] to 0 after each dispatch, forcing a new marker read on the next loop iteration
High markers 220 and 221 dispatch to StreamingDataReader and StreamRead2ByteTokenParser, and marker 219 to MP3HuffmanDecoder
APP markers 224..239 dispatch through the function table at this+0x190 indexed by (4*marker - 880), and marker 254 (COM) dispatches through the handler pointer at *(this+0x190+12) (this+0x19C)
Marker 216 (SOI) dispatches to sub_50FF84 for context initialization
Markers 1 and 208..215 use the parameterized dispatch: write state code 91 to obj+0x14, the marker to obj+0x18, and dispatch through obj vtable slot 1 with argument 1
Marker 217 writes state code 84 to obj+0x14, dispatches through obj vtable slot 1 with argument 1, and returns 2
Remaining markers in the 208..218 range (default path) dispatch to sub_51030D; a non-zero result returns 1, otherwise 0
Unrecognized markers (2..191, 222/223, 240..253, 255): write state code 67 to obj+0x14, the marker to obj+0x18, and dispatch through obj vtable slot 0

unresolved: The dispatch-table walk for markers 224..239 at (this[100] + 4*marker - 880) references table entries not statically known from this packet; the table content and per-APP-handler behavior are unresolved
Marker 217 returns 2 while marker 1 / 208..215 path returns through the outer loop; the return-value contract (0/1/2) across callers is not established here
The reader-config object at this+0x190 also serves as the dispatch base and byte-stuffing flag holder; whether it is a dedicated config struct or a shared context is unresolved

The marker-distance arithmetic (201..205) leaves the 204-to-sub_510975 and 205-or-above-to-error routes overlapping in a way that suggests the decompiler structure, not clearly distinct semantic states
